column1: # *** THE 1999 DEATHS, TESTED AGAINST THE FREE GAZETTE - 17 September 2026. ***
# Worklist row 122 asked whether 12 November 1999 can be confirmed, and row 11 asked whether the
# gendatabase cluster of 1999s is a catastrophe or an index artefact. NAAIRS was down all day
# (503, no server available), so this is what the free Government Gazette can and cannot settle.
# *** THE HEADLINE: the artefact reading is dead for three of the five, and the four absences are
# worth NOTHING - a control proves this sweep misses real adult deaths. ***

column2: Died *** 1 April 1998 ***, buried Braamfontein - an exact date from cemetery records, in the register as CONNECTED. Roque Luis Armando's second wife, and it was she who signed his 1973 death notice.
column3: *** NO ESTATE. *** Swept for the surname LERENA across the whole 1994-2023 run and she is not there.
column4: *** THIS IS THE CONTROL, AND IT DECIDES HOW THE REST OF THIS FILE READS. *** A documented adult Lerena death, well inside the window, produces no gazette estate at all. *** So absence from this source is not evidence of anything. *** Nothing below may be read as arguing that a person did not die.

column2: *** Two independent sources. *** The GEDCOM gives b. 10 May 1948, d. *** 12 November 1999 *** - an exact day. The gendatabase index separately carries 1999.
column3: *** ESTATE FOUND, AND TWICE: *** GG 20821, 28 January 2000, p.41, Transvaal; re-advertised GG 20926, 3 March 2000, p.76.
column4: *** CORROBORATED, AND THIS IS THE ROW THAT KILLS THE ARTEFACT READING. *** An official government notice ten weeks after the claimed date is independent of both genealogical sources. *** A default or padded year does not reproduce as an exact day in a separate source and then land ten weeks before a real gazette notice. *** His 1999 is real.

column2: The same GEDCOM, b. 2 January 1986, dead *** the same day as his father ***, aged thirteen.
column3: No estate - *** and none was ever expected. ***
column4: *** UNCORROBORATED, BUT THE ABSENCE IS MEANINGLESS. *** A minor child with no assets is not given a J193 advertisement. *** The gazette was never capable of testing him. *** His date rests on the GEDCOM, which is right about his father to the week.

column2: The same GEDCOM, b. 2 January 1991, dead *** the same day ***, aged eight.
column3: No estate, for the same reason.
column4: *** UNCORROBORATED, ABSENCE MEANINGLESS. *** Same as his brother. *** What can be said is that a single source placing a father and two sons dead on one named day is internally consistent and is correct about the one member of the three the gazette can check. ***

column2: *** One index row only. *** The gendatabase gives her 1999. The GEDCOM names her as the boys' mother and does *** not *** give her a death.
column4: *** OPEN, AND THE ABSENCE PROVES NOTHING TWICE OVER. *** First, Rhena May above. *** Second, a wife married in community of property shares ONE joint estate, wound up in the husband's name - so even had she died with them, the expected number of separate advertisements is exactly the one already found. *** Her 1999 still rests on a single index row and must not be published as fact.

column2: *** One index row only ***, b.1952, carrying 1999.
column3: *** SHE WAS NEVER IN THE SEARCH. *** The sweep was keyed on the surname *** LERENA ***; this index has her under *** KARON ***.
column4: *** NOT A NULL - A FALSE NULL AVERTED. *** Reporting her absence as a tested absence would have been a straight error, because the search key could not have found her whatever the truth. *** Anyone re-running this must sweep KARON as well. *** Her 1999 is untested, not absent.

column1: *** CALIBRATION: how long does an estate take to reach the gazette? ***
column2: Every Lerena where a true death date is known from elsewhere, against the year it was advertised.
column3: Ricardo Juan Carlos: died 21 Dec 1994, advertised *** March 1996 *** (15 months). Paul Raymond: died 2000, advertised *** Feb 2001 *** (13 months). Doreen May: 1999 per the index, advertised *** Feb 2001 and again Nov 2002 ***. Anton Armando: died 3 Apr 2003, advertised *** Aug 2013 *** - *** ten years. *** Pierre Frederick: 12 Nov 1999, advertised *** Jan 2000 *** - ten weeks.
column4: *** THE LAG RUNS FROM TEN WEEKS TO TEN YEARS, AND SOMETIMES AN ESTATE NEVER APPEARS. *** This is why the gazette year was never a death year, and it is why no absence in this file carries weight. *** Record it so the next person does not have to rediscover it. ***

column2: Rows 122 and 11 both need a death REGISTRATION, not an estate notice.

column2: This table was built on 17 September from the Government Gazette, which could not reach Gayle, the two children, or Catherine.
column3: *** The Johannesburg cemetery register reaches them. *** Pierre Frederick and Richard: *** death 12 November 1999. *** Gayle and Jeffrey: *** buried 22 November 1999. *** All four: *** burial registration 18 November 1999 ***, and *** four consecutive record identifiers. *** Doreen May: *** died 17 November 1999. ***
column4: *** THE VERDICTS BELOW STAND AS REASONING AND ARE OVERTAKEN AS CONCLUSIONS. *** In particular the line that Gayle's 1999 *** 'rests on a single index row and must not be published as fact' *** was right when written and is now closed by a second, independent, free source. *** The artefact hypothesis is dead for four of the five, and the fifth - Catherine Tertia Karon - is still untested because she is indexed under KARON. *** See the cemetery table on this page.
